Challenging the award dated 26/06/2019 passed by the 2nd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District - Rajnandgaon (CG) in Claim Case No.181/2015, the appellants / claimants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act').

sentences.text: 2. By the impugned award, against a claim of Rs.3,40,000/-, learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,87,000/- in favour of the appellant / claimant on account of injuries sustained Khilesh Kumar vs Shatrughan Singh on 8 May, 2024

1 by him in an accident that occurred on 22/10/2014.

The appellant and his brother was going on motor cycle to village - Telinbandha and dashed to the offending vehicle (truck) bearing registration No.CG 07 CA/7339 which was parked on wrong side of the road (without any sign or indicator) by respondent No.1 /
driver, owned by respondent No.2 and Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16773 insured with respondent No.3/insurance company.

3. As per pleadings of the claim application, on account of the said accident, the appellant suffered severe injuries on different parts of his body and also sustained fracture and suffered permanent disablement.
He had no money for treatment of fracture, therefore he took herbal cure.

Therefore,
the abovestated compensation was claimed.
The respondents resisted the claim application on various grounds.
4. On the basis of pleadings of the parties, learned Tribunal framed issues and decided the same in favour of the appellant / claimant and against the respondents.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant / claimant submits that the amount of compensation is meager.
It is submitted that 50% disability certificate was filed by the appellant, however, learned Tribunal has wrongly assessed functional disability to 25%.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 supports the award and submits that in a given facts and circumstances available on record, just compensation has been awarded.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submission and perused the records.
8. Considering that the appellant has suffered permanent disablement on his left leg, the assessment of functional disability of 25% by the Tribunal appears to be on the lower side.
Therefore, the same is enhanced to 40%.
Considering the age of the appellant ; nature of job and minimum wages, his monthly income is assessed to Rs.5,500/-.
Accordingly, this Court reassesses the compensation in the following manner - 1

Monthly income Rs.5500/-
2 Future Prospects 25% (5500+2200) Rs.7700/-
3 Yearly loss of income (7700 x 12) Rs.92400/-

Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16773 4 Functional disability and loss of Rs.23100/-
earning capacity (92400 x 25%) 5 Applying Multiplier of 18 (23100 x 18) Rs.4,15,800/-
(Loss of future earning)
Khilesh Kumar vs Shatrughan Singh on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32096867/

2 6. Medical treatment + Rs.2,000/-
7. Loss of earning during treatment + Rs.16500/-
8. Physical and mental agony + Rs.10000/-
9. Nutritional diet and Transportation exp. + Rs.10000/-
TOTAL COMPENSATION Rs.454300/-
9.
The learned Tribunal awarded Rs.1,87,000/- which is deducted from the total compensation now assessed and the enhanced compensation comes to Rs.2,67,300/-.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, interest @ 6% is also awarded on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of this order to be deposited by the insurance company within a period of 60 days.
After deposit, 90% of the amount be invested as fixed deposit in the name of the appellant in a nationalised bank for two years.
Remaining 10% shall be paid to appellant through Bank transaction / account payee cheque.
10. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed.
